Internal helper: the generalized VIF of each set of dummy variables

Source: R/models.R
dot-jst_compute_gvif.Rd

A categorical predictor of three or more categories enters a model as a set of dummy variables, and the VIF table gave each dummy column its own VIF, which depends on the reference category; car::vif() gives the set one generalized VIF (Fox and Monette, 1992; the S346 item, built Session 375): det(R11) * det(R22) / det(R), R the predictors' correlation matrix, R11 the set's block and R22 the rest's, with GVIF^(1/(2*Df)) beside it – on the scale of the square root of a VIF, so its square compares with the usual VIF guidelines. A set is a multi-category predictor's dummy columns and, in a model with an interaction, the interaction columns built on them with the same other variables (Age * Region). Any other column is a set of one, whose GVIF is its VIF.

Usage

.jst_compute_gvif(model, regs)

Arguments

model

A fitted lm or glm.

regs

The multi-category registrations, .jst_collect_multicat_regs().

Value

NULL when no set has two or more columns (the table is then the plain VIF table), or when the correlation matrix is singular; otherwise a data frame of term, GVIF, Df and GVIF_adj (GVIF^(1/(2*Df))), in the model's column order.

References

Fox, J., and Monette, G. (1992). Generalized collinearity diagnostics. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 87(417), 178-183.
